For the fiscal year December 31 2022, the city has a preliminary deficit of 10.99 million. This amount includes the December 22 snow event costs of 1.97 million.
Some of the larger contributing factors to this deficit are an overall deficit within the snow and ice management program of 6.03 million.

Yes, in diesel deficits of 1.94 million, lower than expected revenues in leisure centers and parking. However, the city did have surprises within the municipal revenue sharing revenue higher than budget transit revenues and higher interest and investment income along with 3.25 million in discretionary savings.
After deducting the borrowing improved at the December 22 snow event, the deficit remaining to be funded was 9.02 million.
As recommended in the report, administration has presented a strong financial plan to offset the shortfall through numerous reserves that I will speak to in a few slides. Next slide please.
Overall, the utility programs had a surplus of 3.16 million with all utilities coming into the surplus except for the water utility.
The utility surpluses or deficits have been transferred to or from the respective utility stabilization capital or replacement reserves as outlined in policy. Next slide please.
All through 2022, the city administration looked for several ways to keep costs down on training and discretionary spending.
As just mentioned, through these measures, administration saved $3.25 million.

The administration reduced these expenses with an across the board directive for all departments due to lower revenues and other budgetary pressures, such as fuel costs and overall inflation that the city has experienced. Next slide.

For 2022, the snow and ice management program was in a deficit of 6.03 million. This includes the 1.97 million from the December snow event and also a transfer that is already completed from the snow and ice management contingency reserve of 488,000,500.

For budget, it was estimated that there would be an average of about 5 snow events for a calendar year and in early 2022 to late fall, Saskatoon had 8 events with high snow accumulation followed by the December 2022 snow events for a total of 10 events in the year.

The 1.97 million costs from the December snow event will be funded through borrowing with repayment plan options to be presented to city council for deliberation at the 24 budget deliberation meeting. Next slide please.
Following the deduction of the 1.97 million, there remains about 9 million to be funded in deficit.
Administration has recommended that city council wave 3 transfers to reserves, so the surpluses within these programs can help to offset the deficit.
They are the animal services program, the U-Sport subsidy and the internal audit program. Next slide.
During 2022 for capital projects return funds to the paved roadways infrastructure reserve in the amount of 710,740 dollars.
These were older projects whose work was complete and came in under budget.

As the paved roadways infrastructure reserve received these surpluses funds, administration is recommending a reduction in the transfer from the roadways operating program to the paved roadways infrastructure reserve in the amount of the 710,740 dollars.
This will help offset the overall deficit. This transfer does not impact the work expected to be completed within the 23 roadways program. Next slide please.
During 2022 Saskatoon land operations administration fees that were received from $93.6 million of land sales resulted in an operating surplus of 2.8 million,
which was transferred to the land operations reserve, bringing the reserve over the maximum allowable by the policy.
Therefore, an additional amount of 2.5 million was subsequently transferred from this reserve to the property realized reserve.
Administration is recommending that a one-time transfer be completed from the land operations reserve in the amount of 924,395 dollars to help offset the overall deficit.
Land operations is not anticipating a deficit for 2023, therefore the use of these funds should not impact the 23 operations. Next slide please.
Due to the COVID-19 impact of the number of events during 2020 and 2021, the special events reserve profile Saskatoon portion of that reserve has a balance of $1.35 million as at December 31 2022.
It is expected that one-time transfer from this reserve in the amount of 500,000 can be completed while still leaving the reserve with sufficient funds to cover the 23 expected events.
Therefore, this is being recommended by the Administration. Next slide please.
And finally, the Administration is recommending that the remaining deficit of 6.68 million be funded from the fiscal stabilization reserve.
This will leave a zero dollar balance within that reserve at the end of December 2022.
However, at the 23 budget deliberation meeting, City Council did a proven amount of 1.64 million be transferred into the fiscal stabilization reserve in 23.
Therefore, in 23, that balance of 1.64 million is available for any potential 20-23 deficits.
And I am available for any questions that you might have.

What I would call a safety net for the EBS and flows and budget obviously we budget based on the best information we have at the time.

We're going to have deficits.

We have surpluses.
